speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to begin our assessment, how old are you and exactly how did this swelling start?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (Oligoarticular type).

Given the patient's age, unilateral knee swelling without trauma, and a strong family history suggestive of a genetic link, this presentation is highly characteristic of oligoarticular JIA. I recommend ordering an Antinuclear Antibody (ANA) test and checking inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP) to confirm the diagnosis and assess disease activity. REQUEST TEST: ANA, ESR, CRP.
